questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Divergence of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (F+2G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡{y}^{2}\,j,\,∇\cdot G=-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F+2G) & =∇\cdot F+∇\cdot (2G) \\  & =∇\cdot F+2∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{2y}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{2}{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F+2G) & =∇\cdot F+2∇\cdot G \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{2}{y}+2\cdot (-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{2}{y}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{2}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{y}+\frac{2}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2y}{{y}^{2}}+\frac{2}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2(1+y)}{{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Divergence of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the following identity:

$$
∇\cdot (f\,F)=f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f
$$

First, we compute $∇\cdot F$ and $∇f.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨1,0⟩, \\ ∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{-x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-y{e}^{y})=-y{e}^{-x}-{e}^{y}-y{e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (f\,F) & =f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f \\  & =x(-y{e}^{-x}-{e}^{y}-y{e}^{y})+⟨y{e}^{-x},-y{e}^{y}⟩\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =-yx{e}^{-x}-x{e}^{y}-yx{e}^{y}+y{e}^{-x} \\  & =y{e}^{-x}-yx{e}^{-x}-x{e}^{y}-yx{e}^{y} \\  & =y(1-x){e}^{-x}-x(1+y){e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Divergence of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the following identity:

$$
∇\cdot (f\,F)=f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f
$$

First, we compute $∇\cdot F$ and $∇f.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨2xy,{x}^{2}⟩, \\ ∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y)=y+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (f\,F) & =f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f \\  & ={x}^{2}y(y+2)+⟨xy,2y⟩\cdot ⟨2xy,{x}^{2}⟩ \\  & ={x}^{2}{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y+2{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y \\  & =3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+4{x}^{2}y \\  & ={x}^{2}y(3y+4).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Divergence of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (2F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F=2x{e}^{y}\,i-({e}^{y}+yz)\,j+({z}^{2}+{x}^{3})\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (2F)=2∇\cdot F.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{e}^{y})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-({e}^{y}+yz))+\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{2}+{x}^{3}) \\  & =2{e}^{y}-{e}^{y}-z+2z \\  & ={e}^{y}+z.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (2F) & =2∇\cdot F \\  & =2\cdot ({e}^{y}+z) \\  & =2{e}^{y}+2z.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Divergence of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F+4G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F={x}^{2}{y}^{3}\,i+{y}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,j,\,∇\cdot G=-\frac{1}{2}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F+4G) & =∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F)+∇\cdot (4G) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}∇\cdot F+4∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{3})+\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =2x{y}^{3}+2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F+2G) & =\frac{1}{2}∇\cdot F+4∇\cdot G \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2x{y}^{3}+2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+4\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}y\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =x{y}^{3}+y\operatorname{ln}⁡x-2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =x{y}^{3}-y\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
